cashTip: Cards and contactless work almost everywhere; carry a few euros for cafés, markets and small boats.
name: Lagos · Algarve
tagline: Golden cliffs, sea caves and Algarve beaches
summary: Lagos is the liveliest base on Portugal's Algarve coast, with a walled old town, golden sea stacks at Ponta da Piedade and beautiful cove beaches. From here you can kayak into sea caves, visit Benagil, hike the clifftop Seven Hanging Valleys trail and reach Europe's south-western tip at Sagres.
seasonNote: June and September are warm and less crowded than July and August. Spring is green and great for hiking. Winter is mild and quiet.
arrival: Faro Airport is about 1 hour by car. Trains and buses link Lisbon in about 4 hours.
gettingAround: Walk the town; a rental car for beaches; boats and kayaks for the coast.
foodTip: Cataplana seafood stew, grilled sardines and piri-piri chicken.
buyTip: Cork goods, painted tiles and medronho brandy.

connections.note: Train or bus; about 3 hours by car.

items.name: Ponta da Piedade
items.summary: Golden sea stacks, arches and grottoes, seen from cliff paths or by boat.
items.expect: Stairs lead down to the water.
items.tip: Take a kayak or small boat into the grottoes.

items.name: Benagil Cave
items.summary: A sea cave with a hole in its dome lighting a hidden beach.
items.expect: Landing inside is no longer allowed; view by boat or kayak.
items.tip: Go early to avoid boat traffic.

items.name: Praia da Marinha
items.summary: A cove beach of honey-coloured cliffs and clear water.
items.expect: Steps down from the car park.

items.name: Seven Hanging Valleys trail
items.summary: A 6 km cliff walk from Praia da Marinha to Vale Centeanes.

items.name: Old town and walls
items.summary: Cobbled lanes, city walls and the old slave market museum.

items.name: Sagres and Cape St Vincent
items.summary: Windswept cliffs at Europe's south-west corner, with a lighthouse and fortress.

items.name: Praia Dona Ana
items.summary: A small beach framed by rock stacks, walkable from town.

items.name: Cataplana
items.summary: Seafood stewed in a copper clam-shaped pot.

items.name: Grilled sardines
items.summary: Fresh sardines grilled over charcoal with bread and salad.

items.name: Piri-piri chicken
items.summary: Charcoal chicken with fiery piri-piri oil, famous in nearby Guia.

cashTip: Cards and contactless work almost everywhere; carry a few euros for cafés, markets and small boats.
name: Funchal · Madeira
tagline: Madeira's capital of flowers, levadas and wine
summary: Funchal is the capital of Madeira, a lush Atlantic island of cliffs, mountains and gardens. Ride a cable car up to Monte and toboggan down in a wicker sled, walk levada irrigation channels through laurel forest, hike between the highest peaks and taste Madeira wine.
seasonNote: Mild year-round. Spring brings the Flower Festival. New Year's Eve fireworks are world-famous. The north is wetter than the south.
arrival: Madeira Airport is 25 minutes from Funchal with flights from Lisbon (under 2 hours) and across Europe.
gettingAround: Walk Funchal; rent a car or join tours for the island.
foodTip: Espetada beef skewers, black scabbard fish with banana, bolo do caco bread and poncha.
baseArea: Funchal old town or the Lido

items.name: Monte cable car and toboggan
items.summary: A cable car up to Monte's palace gardens, then a ride down in a wicker toboggan steered by men in straw hats.
items.tip: Visit Monte Palace gardens before the toboggan.

items.name: Mercado dos Lavradores
items.summary: A tiled market of exotic fruit, flowers and a fish hall.
items.tip: Visit the fish hall for scabbard fish.

items.name: Zona Velha old town
items.summary: Lanes of painted doors, bars and restaurants.

items.name: Levada walk
items.summary: Walks along irrigation channels through laurel forest to waterfalls, such as 25 Fontes.
items.expect: Wear good shoes; some routes need a torch.

items.name: Pico do Arieiro to Pico Ruivo
items.summary: A dramatic ridge hike between Madeira's highest peaks above the clouds.
items.expect: Check trail status; some sections close.

items.name: Cabo Girão skywalk
items.summary: A glass platform on one of Europe's highest sea cliffs.
items.tip: Stop at Câmara de Lobos for poncha.

items.name: Porto Moniz pools
items.summary: Natural volcanic rock pools filled by the Atlantic.
items.tip: Combine with the north coast drive.

items.name: Espetada
items.summary: Garlic beef skewers hung from a stand, with fried maize.
items.tip: Order milho frito on the side.

items.name: Black scabbard fish with banana
items.summary: Fried deep-sea fish served with banana and passion fruit sauce.

items.name: Poncha and bolo do caco
items.summary: Sugar-cane rum with honey and lemon, plus garlic-butter flatbread.
items.tip: Try the original at Câmara de Lobos.

cashTip: Cards and contactless work almost everywhere; carry a few euros for cafés, markets and small boats.
name: Ponta Delgada · Azores
tagline: Crater lakes, hot springs and whales mid-Atlantic
summary: Ponta Delgada is the gateway to São Miguel, the largest island of the Azores. Volcanic crater lakes, steaming hot springs, tea plantations and whale-watching trips make it one of Europe's best nature escapes.
seasonNote: Summer is warmest and calmest. Weather changes fast all year; bring layers. Whales are seen year-round, with most species in spring.
arrival: Ponta Delgada Airport has flights from Lisbon (about 2 hours) and some from North America.
gettingAround: Rent a car; buses are limited.
foodTip: Cozido das Furnas cooked in volcanic ground, limpets, local cheese and pineapple.
buyTip: Gorreana tea, Azorean pineapples and São Jorge cheese.

items.name: Sete Cidades lakes
items.summary: Twin blue and green lakes in a huge volcanic crater.
items.expect: Cloud can hide the view; check webcams.
items.tip: See it from Vista do Rei.

items.name: Furnas hot springs
items.summary: A valley of fumaroles, thermal pools and stews cooked underground.
items.expect: Bring an old swimsuit; iron water stains.
items.tip: Bathe in Poça da Dona Beija at night.

items.name: Lagoa do Fogo
items.summary: A wild crater lake with white beaches, high in the mountains.
items.expect: Viewpoint off the road; trail down.

items.name: Whale watching
items.summary: Boat trips to see sperm whales, dolphins and seasonal blue whales.
items.why: One of the world's best whale spots.

items.name: Terra Nostra Garden
items.summary: Botanical gardens with a warm iron-orange thermal pool.

items.name: Gorreana tea plantation
items.summary: Europe's oldest tea plantation, still working with free tastings.

items.name: Portas da Cidade
items.summary: Triple-arched city gates and black-and-white basalt streets.

items.name: Cozido das Furnas
items.summary: Meat and vegetables slow-cooked for hours in volcanic ground.

items.name: Lapas (limpets)
items.summary: Grilled limpets with garlic butter and lemon.
items.tip: Mop up the butter with bread.

items.name: Azorean pineapple and queijadas
items.summary: Pineapples grown in glasshouses, plus sweet cheese tarts.

cashTip: Cards are widely accepted; carry euro cash for ferries, markets and small konobas.
name: Split
tagline: A living Roman palace on the Dalmatian coast
summary: Split's old town grew inside the walls of Roman Emperor Diocletian's palace, where cafés now fill 1,700-year-old courtyards. It's Croatia's ferry hub for islands like Hvar and Brač, with Krka's waterfalls and medieval Trogir nearby.
seasonNote: June and September are warm with fewer crowds. July and August are hot and packed. Winter is quiet and mild.
arrival: Split Airport is 30 minutes away. Buses from Zagreb take about 5 hours; ferries link the islands.
gettingAround: Walk the centre; buses and ferries for day trips.
foodTip: Pašticada beef stew, black risotto, burek and peka.
buyTip: Olive oil, lavender, wine and local jewellery.

items.name: Diocletian's Palace
items.summary: A 4th-century Roman palace whose walls hold the old town, with cellars and the Peristyle.
items.expect: Free to wander; cellars have a fee.
items.tip: Visit the cellars, then the Peristyle at night.

items.name: Cathedral of St Domnius
items.summary: Diocletian's mausoleum turned cathedral, with a bell tower to climb.
items.why: The oldest cathedral building in use.

items.name: Riva promenade
items.summary: A palm-lined seafront of cafés facing the harbour.
items.tip: Have coffee here in the morning.

items.name: Marjan hill
items.summary: A forested hill with views, chapels and swimming coves.
items.tip: Climb to the first viewpoint at sunset.

items.name: Trogir
items.summary: A medieval island town of churches and palaces.

items.name: Krka National Park
items.summary: Cascading waterfalls and boardwalks over turquoise pools.

items.name: Klis Fortress
items.summary: A clifftop fortress used as Meereen in Game of Thrones.

items.name: Pašticada
items.summary: Beef marinated and slow-cooked in wine and prunes, with gnocchi.

items.name: Black risotto
items.summary: Risotto coloured black with cuttlefish ink.

items.name: Burek
items.summary: Flaky pastry filled with cheese or meat.

cashTip: Cards are widely accepted; carry euro cash for ferries, markets and small konobas.
name: Zagreb
tagline: Croatia's café-loving capital with a quirky streak
summary: Zagreb is a walkable Central European capital of Austro-Hungarian squares, a hilltop Upper Town with a tiled-roof church, lively markets and cafés. Its famous Advent market is one of Europe's best, and Plitvice Lakes is a day trip away.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are pleasant. December brings award-winning Advent markets. Summer is warm and quieter.
arrival: Zagreb Airport is 25 minutes by bus. Trains and buses link Ljubljana, Vienna and Budapest.
gettingAround: Walk the centre; trams cover the city.
foodTip: Štrukli cheese pastry, ćevapi and kremšnita custard cake.
buyTip: Licitar hearts, neckties (the cravat is Croatian) and local brandies.
baseArea: Lower Town near Ban Jelačić Square

items.name: St Mark's Church and Upper Town
items.summary: A church with a colourful tiled roof in the medieval Upper Town.
items.expect: Exterior only most of the time.

items.name: Museum of Broken Relationships
items.summary: Objects and stories donated by people after break-ups.

items.name: Dolac market
items.summary: An open-air market under red umbrellas, with a hall below.

items.name: Zagreb Cathedral
items.summary: Twin-spired Gothic cathedral, under restoration since the 2020 earthquake.

items.name: Ban Jelačić Square
items.summary: The main square, a meeting point ringed by cafés.

items.name: Mirogoj Cemetery
items.summary: An arcaded cemetery park, one of Europe's most beautiful.

items.name: Tkalčićeva Street
items.summary: A curving street of bars and cafés built over an old stream.
items.tip: Have a drink in the evening.

items.name: Štrukli
items.summary: Dough filled with fresh cheese, boiled or baked with cream.

items.name: Ćevapi
items.summary: Grilled minced meat fingers with flatbread and onions.

items.name: Kremšnita
items.summary: Custard and cream cake in flaky pastry.

cashTip: Cards are widely accepted; carry euro cash for ferries, markets and small konobas.
name: Plitvice Lakes
tagline: Sixteen turquoise lakes linked by waterfalls
summary: Plitvice Lakes is Croatia's oldest national park: 16 terraced lakes in shades of turquoise, joined by waterfalls and crossed by wooden boardwalks through the forest. It's one of Europe's most beautiful natural sights.
seasonNote: Spring has the most water; autumn the best colours. Summer is crowded and tickets cost more. Winter brings frozen falls.
arrival: Buses from Zagreb take about 2.5 hours and from Split about 4. Stay nearby to arrive at opening.
gettingAround: Park boats and electric trains link the trails; included in the ticket.
foodTip: Grilled trout, spit-roast lamb and Lika potatoes.

items.name: Lower Lakes and Veliki Slap
items.summary: Canyon lakes, boardwalks and the 78 m Great Waterfall.
items.tip: Enter at opening, around 7 am in summer.

items.name: Upper Lakes
items.summary: Terraced lakes and dozens of cascades through beech forest.
items.expect: Long walk; follow route C or H.
items.tip: Do the Upper Lakes after the boat.

items.name: Kozjak Lake boat
items.summary: An electric boat across the park's largest lake.

items.name: Panorama viewpoint
items.summary: The famous overhead view of the lower lakes and waterfalls.
items.tip: Come back late afternoon for soft light.

items.name: Rastoke
items.summary: A village of old watermills built over waterfalls.

items.name: Barać Caves
items.summary: Guided tours through limestone caves.

items.name: Grilled trout
items.summary: Local trout grilled with garlic and potatoes.

items.name: Spit-roast lamb
items.summary: Whole lamb roasted on a spit at roadside restaurants.

items.name: Cheese štrukli
items.summary: Cheese-filled pastry, baked with cream.

cashTip: Cards are widely accepted; carry euro cash for ferries, markets and small konobas.
name: Hvar
tagline: Lavender, yachts and a Venetian harbour town
summary: Hvar is Croatia's sunniest island, with a Venetian harbour town under a hilltop fortress, lavender fields, vineyards and the Pakleni islands offshore. It's known for chic nightlife but also has quiet villages and the UNESCO-listed Stari Grad Plain.
seasonNote: June and September are ideal. July and August are packed and party-heavy. Lavender blooms in late June.
arrival: Catamarans from Split reach Hvar town in about 1 hour; car ferries go to Stari Grad.
gettingAround: Walk Hvar town; scooters, taxis and water taxis.
foodTip: Gregada fish stew, peka and Plavac Mali red wine.
buyTip: Lavender oil and sachets, and local wine.
baseArea: Hvar town or quieter Stari Grad

items.name: Fortica fortress
items.summary: A Venetian-Spanish fortress above town with sweeping views.

items.name: St Stephen's Square
items.summary: One of Dalmatia's largest squares, with the cathedral and harbour.
items.tip: Have coffee here in the morning.

items.name: Pakleni Islands
items.summary: Pine-covered islets with coves and beach clubs, by water taxi.
items.expect: Taxis leave the harbour all day.

items.name: Lavender fields
items.summary: Hillside lavender around an old village, with a June festival.

items.name: Stari Grad Plain
items.summary: Ancient Greek field divisions still farmed after 2,400 years.

items.name: Hvar Theatre and Arsenal
items.summary: One of Europe's oldest public theatres, from 1612.

items.name: Blue Cave
items.summary: A sea cave glowing electric blue at midday.

items.name: Gregada
items.summary: A white fish stew with potatoes and olive oil.

items.name: Peka
items.summary: Lamb or octopus slow-cooked under a bell of embers.

items.name: Plavac Mali wine
items.summary: Bold local red wine at village wineries.
